title: My friends
grammar: His name is… / Her name is…

scene.speaker: tomas
scene.bubble: This is my best friend Nico. His jokes are terrible… and that's why we laugh so much!
scene.intro: This is my best friend, says Tomás. His name is Nico and his jokes are terrible — that is why we laugh! Freya smiles: this is my friend too. Her name is Astrid and she is very kind, she always shares her crayons. Friends play together, friends share, friends are funny. What is YOUR friend's name? Say his name, say her name, and tell us why he or she is special!

activities.title: Match the friend with the description.

pairs.right: Her hair is yellow. She asks questions.
His jokes are funny. He smiles a lot.
His football is always with him.

activities.title: Listen. Who are the new friends? Write a name or word in each gap.

data.script: Tomas: This is my new friend. His name is Leo. He plays football very well! … Freya: And this is Emma. Her name is on her bag — E-M-M-A. … Tomas: Leo's favourite colour is green, like his cap. … Freya: Emma has got a little dog. Its name is Toto. … Tomas: We all play together at break. … Freya: Friends make school the best place!

data.text: Present your partner to another pair: "This is… His/Her name is… He/She likes…" Two sentences each!

activities.title: Spot the differences!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 11 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Draw your best friend and write 4 sentences: His/Her name is… He/She likes…

outcomes.puede: Understand short simple dialogues about family, school, animals, food (Cambridge Starters Listening parts 1–4).
Answer picture-prompted questions; describe a picture in simple sentences.
Read 2–3-sentence texts; match pictures to words and short captions.
Copy words and complete short sentences (Starters Reading/Writing parts).
~450 words (Starters wordlist); Present simple, present continuous (limited), there is/are, like + -ing.
